subject.title: [Feature]: GitHub Copilot provider cannot reach GitHub Enterprise data-residency (*.ghe.com) tenants

question: Should OpenClaw accept allowlisted `github.com` and single-label `*.ghe.com` Copilot auth/token routing inside the bundled `github-copilot` provider?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the fix changes credential destination policy, cache scoping, guided setup, and config/env behavior for a bundled provider; automation should not decide that security/product boundary alone.

options.title: Accept narrow bundled-provider GHE routing
options.body: Review and harden the linked PR so existing `github-copilot` users on data-residency tenants get guided setup without a separate provider.

options.title: Require a generic host-routing contract first
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers define a reusable provider-auth host-routing seam and then adapt the implementation to that contract.

options.title: Route GHE Copilot to plugin scope
options.body: Close this issue and the linked PR as out of core scope, preserving the capability for ClawHub or an external provider plugin.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow bundled-provider GHE routing
recommendation.body: Review and harden the linked PR so existing `github-copilot` users on data-residency tenants get guided setup without a separate provider.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent current-main signal on the touched Copilot provider/auth lines and adjacent provider work.
